title: Canary quality gates — talking points & Q&A (lead notes)
content:
Purpose: quick leader-facing notes to frame the new Canary Quality Gates feature during the March all-hands and to seed answers for follow-ups. This is a personal scratchpad — terse, incomplete, intentionally rough.

Topline (1–2 sentences):
- We’re rolling out Canary Quality Gates next week: automated checks that will halt or roll back model rollouts when critical quality regressions are detected against production prompts and perf budgets. Goal: reduce customer-visible regressions and shorten remediation cycles.

Why this matters (for non-engineers):
- Shipping many model variants and quantized builds increased velocity but made regressions more likely. Canary gates give us automated guardrails so product teams can move faster without increasing support burden.

What leaders should say (short bullets to read on stage):
- Quick: "Today we’re launching Canary Quality Gates — automated tests that evaluate new model variants on a small slice of live traffic and block rollouts if quality or latency drops exceed thresholds. This helps us keep products reliable while maintaining speed of iteration."
- Emphasize customer benefit: "Fewer surprises for customers; quicker recovery when something slips through our lab tests."
- Emphasize guardrails not brakes: "These gates are configurable — teams decide the thresholds and can opt into soft vs hard gating during early experiments."

Key features to call out (avoid deep tech on stage):
- Canary slice: small % of traffic, routed to candidate variant.
- Dual metrics: quality (prompt-level evals, A/B scoring) + perf (p99 latency, error rate).
- Auto actions: soft alert / rollback / traffic-shift depending on policy.
- Observability: linked traces & per-prompt regression diffs in Console.

Anticipated questions + short answers (prep for Q&A):
Q: How is this different from current canaries?
A: Current canaries focus on infra/latency. These extend to output quality measured against curated prompt sets + live score deltas. They also support automatic rollback policies based on configurable risk tolerances.

Q: Will teams lose control of rollouts?
A: No — gates are opt-in per rollout. We default to "warning" for first two weeks on any new product rollout and provide clear rollback rationale in the Console. Platform SREs can help teams choose thresholds.

Q: What signals are used for "quality"?
A: Primary signals: model-assigned quality score (reranker/LLM comparator), embedding-distance drift on prompt archetypes, and customer-side error/clarity flags (when available). We also run targeted evaluation prompts from product-maintained suites.

Q: Could this increase false positives (blocking safe changes)?
A: Yes possibility. Mitigations: threshold tuning, soft alerts, human-in-the-loop approvals for high-impact rollouts, and a post-mortem workflow to quickly adjust gate configs.

Q: Who owns the gates?
A: Product team sets the policy for product rollouts; platform provides default templates and SRE supports stability-critical services. Ownership model: product = policy, platform = enforcement/observability.

Ops/Support playbook (short):
- If a rollback occurs: Console shows roll-back cause + sample prompts. On-call follows standard incident checklist: triage -> assess impact -> engage model owners -> hotfix/rollback -> post-mortem.
- Create a short triage template for these rollbacks (Diego to draft).

Open questions / risks (callouts to discuss offline):
- Metric weightings: how do we combine different quality signals into a single pass/fail? (ML research input needed).
- Threshold defaults: product teams will push back if defaults are too strict. Need safe starter presets.
- Privacy: make sure live prompt sampling respects PII opt-out and Private deployment constraints.
- Cost and latency: running additional evals on canary traffic has cost — quantify.

Notes-to-self for the all-hands demo (one minute demo idea):
- Show Console view: rollout > canary slice > gate fired artifact. Use synthetic but realistic example: a paraphrase model variant that increases hallucination on a common prompt set. Show the sample diffs and the one-click rollback.
- Avoid showing raw PII. Redact.

Follow-ups / next steps (owner tags):
- Diego: draft triage template (due Thu).
- Anika: prepare Console screenshots + redacted sample prompts (due Fri).
- Ryan: coordinate demo infra and ensure we have a safe example traffic slice (due Mon).
- Mikaela: finalize leader script and send to exec comms (target Tue morning).

Back-of-envelope metrics to share later (for slides):
- Target: reduce customer-facing regression incidents by 40% in first 3 months.
- Acceptable false-positive rate target: <5% of rollouts.
- Extra cost: approx +3–6% inference CPU/GPU due to evaluation overhead (ballpark, need finance validation).

Stylistic notes (voice):
- Keep it optimistic and concrete. Avoid too much engineering jargon during the live talk. Highlight how this increases developer velocity and customer trust.

Unresolved phrasing for the script (two options):
- Option A (short): "Canary Quality Gates give us automated safety nets — they catch regressions quickly and restore service automatically when needed."
- Option B (longer): "Rather than slowing down releases, we give teams safety tools that automatically test and protect live traffic. Teams still make the call; the platform watches for problems and prevents customers from seeing them."

End of notes. This is rough; will clean up after Diego/Anika/Ryan check their pieces.
